note: ShelfCheck price system cleanup pass. Coverage was measured by loading the live app in a local static-file preview and reading items/priceFor()/huntPrice() directly at runtime (the most reliable way to exercise the real, multi-file price-wrapping chain, since manually replicating ~15 layered price files' fallback order in an offline harness would itself be error-prone). MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: the local preview environment resolved to 2,537 INCLUDED identities rather than the blessed production baseline of 2,542 (a 5-identity / 0.2% gap). Investigated just enough to rule out anything caused by this pass's own changes (git diff confirmed only model-fix.js and price-sort-v063.js were touched, neither reads or writes item.set; both census-integrity-pass-v001.js and census-integrity-pass-v002.js were confirmed applying correctly; data0-3b.txt byte counts matched the repo exactly) before stopping per 'DO NOT reopen or re-audit the census'. The residual gap traces to the census-v052/053/054 PriceCharting-sweep scripts producing slightly fewer identities per-run in this environment than the committed baseline (each phase count was consistently 1-2 lower), which looks like a latent, pre-existing timing/ordering sensitivity in those scripts' own setTimeout-polling readiness checks -- unrelated to price data or this pass's changes. Flagged here as an observation for a future pass, not fixed. Coverage percentages below are computed against the measured 2,537, and are not materially different at the reported precision from what a 2,542 denominator would show.

priceSortBug.cause: model-fix.js's render() has a sort-priority chain (ZA title-desc -> HUNT-filter huntPrice().rank -> search-query acquisitionRank relevance) with no branch for window.SHELFCHECK_SORT==='LOW'/'HIGH'. Whenever a search query was present (or, in principle, any other path that reaches the q-relevance branch), model-fix's render unconditionally re-sorted by acquisitionRank + alphabetical tie-break, discarding the price ordering that price-sort-v063.js's outer render wrapper had already applied to the `items` array -- this is what actually produced the 'looks alphabetized' symptom (confirmed by reproducing it live: filter ALL, sort LOW, search 'a' or 'the' -> results order by acquisitionRank/alpha, ignoring price). Plain ALL/OWNED/NEEDED views with an EMPTY search box were not affected, since model-fix's render leaves `all` in the incoming (already price-sorted) `items` order when no branch fires.
priceSortBug.fix: Exposed price-sort-v063.js's existing numeric comparator as window.SHELFCHECK_PRICE_COMPARE, and added one branch to model-fix.js's render() sort chain -- positioned after the existing ZA and HUNT branches (both left untouched) and before the q-relevance fallback -- that applies it whenever SHELFCHECK_SORT is LOW or HIGH. This makes price sort take priority over search-relevance sort for ALL/OWNED/NEEDED views with a search query active, while the HUNT filter continues to use its own already-correct huntPrice().rank-based comparator (already directionally patched for HIGH by price-sort-v063.js in a prior pass) unchanged.

phase3Findings.productPriceArchitectureGap: No product/compilation-level price field exists anywhere in the codebase (confirmed: no global matching /product.*price/i). Only individual component identities carry prices. This is why 26 of 50 multi-identity products have ZERO priced components and only 11 of 50 have ALL components priced -- there is currently no mechanism to price a compilation at the box level at all, which is itself consistent with (not a violation of) the project rule against assigning one box price to every identity, but means compilation pricing is presently just absent rather than correctly box-level. Flagged as a structural gap for a future feature pass, not built in this cleanup.

externalAccessBlocker.summary: PriceCharting blocks this session's WebFetch tool entirely (HTTP 403 on both the search-products endpoint and individual game pages -- same Cloudflare-style bot-blocking pattern already observed against IGDB in earlier sessions). WebSearch surfaces PriceCharting result URLs and titles but not reliable numeric price figures. No local bulk PriceCharting export is available -- the only local candidate, pricecharting-latest.csv, contains only the placeholder text 'PLACEHOLDER', not real data. The existing tools/price-*.mjs scripts that originally populated the committed price-*.js files use a plain unauthenticated HTTP scrape of pricecharting.com (no API token, no stored credentials anywhere in this repo) -- the same technique this session attempted and found blocked.
externalAccessBlocker.whatWouldUnblockThis: Either (a) Josh runs the existing GitHub Actions price workflows (price-whole-census-fill.yml, price-new-games-*.yml, price-gap-audit.yml) directly, which execute from GitHub's runners rather than this session's environment and are not subject to this local block, or (b) Josh manually exports a real PriceCharting CSV (pricing data > 'download prices') to replace the pricecharting-latest.csv placeholder with actual data for a future local-only matching pass. No credential or token is needed for either path -- this is purely a network-access restriction on this session, not a missing-secret problem.
